title: Temperament and Personality Differences
learningGoal: Help parents understand temperament traits and how to adapt parenting to their child's personality.
microLesson: Temperament describes a child’s natural style—how they react, adapt, and regulate emotions. Some children are cautious, others energetic; some need routine, others are flexible. Understanding temperament helps parents respond with empathy instead of frustration. When parents adapt their approach to the child’s personality, behaviour improves and conflict decreases.
activity: Identify one temperament trait your child shows (e.g., sensitive, active, cautious). Reflect on how you can adapt your parenting to support that trait.
